Codex 0.164.0's keys for a new line in its input box (HI-1327), and how Windows' console delivers the keys Hive presses.
Not a run of Codex.

1. Codex's source at rust-v0.164.0 = 6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9, codex-rs/tui/src/keymap.rs lines 1711-1727
(the composer sends on plain Enter; the editor's insert_newline keys):

                submit: default_bindings![plain(KeyCode::Enter)],
                queue: default_bindings![plain(KeyCode::Tab)],
...
                insert_newline: default_bindings![
                    ctrl(KeyCode::Char('j')),
                    ctrl(KeyCode::Char('m')),
                    plain(KeyCode::Enter),
                    shift(KeyCode::Enter),
                    alt(KeyCode::Enter)
                ],

2. HI-1327's probe (28 Oct 2026): Hive's node-pty (@lydell/node-pty, ConPTY, Windows 11 26200) running a PowerShell
[Console]::ReadKey loop, which reads the console's KEY_EVENT records as crossterm does; bytes written as Hive types:

wrote "\n" (LF)                                  -> KEY key=Enter mods=Control char=10
wrote "\r" (CR)                                  -> KEY key=Enter mods=0 char=13
wrote "\x1b\r" (ESC CR)                          -> KEY key=Enter mods=Alt char=13
wrote "\x1b[74;36;10;1;8;1_\x1b[74;36;10;0;8;1_"  -> KEY key=J mods=Control char=10
wrote "\x1b[13;28;13;1;16;1_\x1b[13;28;13;0;16;1_" -> KEY key=Enter mods=Shift char=13
